# Grid / multi-tier

Contents: [Use cases](#use-cases), [Chart IDs](#chart-ids), [Minimal spec](#minimal-spec), [Data](#data), [Options](#options), [Annotations](#annotations), [Chart IDs and common combinations](#chart-ids-and-common-combinations), [Metric stack](#metric-stack), [Sizing](#sizing), [Fixtures](#fixtures).

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-reference.mjs from the boardplot describe, list and fixtures payloads. -->

Facets, variance tiers and metric stacks with shared categories and computed readouts. Type `grid`. Aliases: `facets`.

## Use cases

- Small multiples per region
- Actuals with a variance tier
- Metric stacks with computed readouts

## Chart IDs

- `grid.panels`: fixture `stacked-plus-dpy`
- `grid.tiers`: fixture `stacked-plus-dpy-tiered`
- `grid.facets`: fixture `facet-regions`
- `grid.metric-stack`: fixture `metric-stack-volume`

## Minimal spec

```json
{
  "type": "grid",
  "data": {
    "panels": [
      {
        "id": "revenue",
        "type": "kpi",
        "data": { "label": "Revenue", "value": 120 },
        "options": { "unit": "$k" }
      },
      {
        "id": "orders",
        "type": "kpi",
        "data": { "label": "Orders", "value": 85 },
        "options": { "unit": "orders" }
      }
    ]
  },
  "options": {
    "sharedScale": false,
    "title": "Revenue is $120k and orders total 85",
    "source": "Illustrative data"
  }
}
```

## Options

| Path | Type | Values | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| stack | object |  |  | Select metric-stack mode of sharedAxis category. Top-down panels, independent zero scales, one axis, one gutter and shared states. |
| stack.heights | array |  |  | Plot heights in layout pixels, one per panel in top-down order. Use rows for proportional heights instead. |
| columns | integer \| array |  |  | Legacy facet column count, or authored positive column-track weights. At most 50 rows and columns. |
| rows | array |  |  | Positive row weights override content fitting. Omitted: content-fit rows use their natural height; other rows share the rest. Without columns, the row count sets placement. With category sharing, rows[i] follows panels[i] in bottom-up order; metric stacks use top-down order. |
| gutters | object |  |  | Uniform or per-gap row/column gutters in pixels. |
| gutters.rows | number \| array |  |  | Vertical spacing between row tracks in layout pixels. |
| gutters.columns | number \| array |  |  | Horizontal spacing between column tracks in layout pixels. |
| anchors | object |  |  | Opt-in shared plot edges, baselines, and category columns by row, column, or all panels. |
| anchors.plotEdges | string | `'row'`, `'column'`, `'all'` |  | Align panel plot left and right edges within column or all groups. row is accepted but ignored: side-by-side plots do not share x edges. |
| anchors.baselines | string | `'row'`, `'column'`, `'all'` |  | Scope for aligning panel numeric baselines vertically. |
| anchors.categories | string | `'row'`, `'column'`, `'all'` |  | column and all align plot x edges and category ticks with authored column centers. row is accepted but ignored: side-by-side plots do not share x edges. |
| alignmentRules | array |  |  | Authored hairline guides bound to a panel plot edge, baseline, or category tick. |
| alignmentRules[].id | string |  |  | Unique guide identifier within this grid. |
| alignmentRules[].orientation | string | `'horizontal'`, `'vertical'` |  | Guide direction; baseline anchors require horizontal, plot-edge and category anchors require vertical. |
| alignmentRules[].at | object |  |  | Panel anchor that fixes the guide coordinate. |
| alignmentRules[].at.panelId | string |  |  | Existing panel that supplies the guide coordinate. |
| alignmentRules[].at.anchor | string | `'plotLeft'`, `'plotRight'`, `'baseline'`, `'category'` |  | Panel plot edge, numeric baseline, or x-axis category tick used to position the guide. |
| alignmentRules[].at.categoryId | string |  |  | Existing x-axis category id; required for a category anchor. |
| alignmentRules[].fromPanelId | string |  |  | Panel whose top or left slot edge starts the guide; omission uses the grid content edge. |
| alignmentRules[].toPanelId | string |  |  | Panel whose bottom or right slot edge ends the guide; omission uses the grid content edge. |
| sharedAxis | string | `'category'`, `'none'` |  | Metric stacks imply category and use top-down order with independent scales. Otherwise default: category only for exactly one column panel plus one or more variance panels (no integrated variance); none otherwise. none honours columns and array order. category uses one column in bottom-up order with the category-axis owner at the bottom; it warns if columns or panelOrder are overridden. These column/variance tiers use 4:1 plot heights unless authored tracks or a shared y scale apply. |
| sharedScale | boolean |  |  | Default: panels share one y scale in every sharedAxis mode only with evidence that they show one measure: every numeric panel names the same non-empty unit and format, the grid names a unit, or the panels come from repeat or a scaleGroup. Without that evidence each panel keeps its own scale, also when all panels are the same chart type. Set true to share panels without a unit, false for independent panel domains. Metric stacks always use independent zero scales and refuse true. |
| panelOrder | string | `'sheet'`, `'lastDesc'`, `'lastAsc'`, `'totalDesc'`, `'totalAsc'` |  | Facet panel order: 'sheet' keeps the authored array (default), 'last*' ranks by each panel's final value, 'total*' by its sum. Panels with no measurable value stay last in both directions. |
| reflow | boolean |  |  | Facets only: a grid of more panels than a numeric columns count, on a card under 480 px, takes columns as a maximum. Where a panel drops category names for room, it draws with fewer columns, down to two, at the largest count that prints every name and that an authored height seats. Default true; false keeps the authored count. |

Plus the [shared options](options.md). This type does not accept `detailFields`, `labels`, `categoryLabels`, `valueAxis.tickStep`, `valueAxis.log`, `valueAxis.reverse`, `valueAxis.break`, `categoryAxis`, `secondaryAxis`, `rowLabels`, `sort`, `topN`, `bandFraction`, `story`, `colorblindSafe`, `rounding`.

## Annotations

This type takes no annotations.

## Chart IDs and common combinations

A grid draws one of four chart IDs, set by its data and options. `grid.tiers`: two or more panels stacked on one shared category axis, `sharedAxis: 'category'`; variance panels under a base chart get it by default. `grid.facets`: small multiples, two or more columns of panels of one chart type that fills its slot, written out in `panels` or repeated from one template through `data.repeat`. `grid.metric-stack`: shared `measures` over shared `categories`, with `stack: {}`. `grid.panels`: every other grid, such as a mix of chart types, a single panel or an authored layout.

The grid key merges entries of different panels only when they have the same label and draw the same colour. Series ids do not matter: two panels that name a series alike and colour it alike share one key entry, and the same label in two colours gives two entries.

Common combinations are recipes, not chart types. Stacked revenue over a ΔPY% variance tier is `grid.tiers` (fixture `stacked-plus-dpy-tiered`). Small multiples by region are `grid.facets` (fixture `facet-regions`, or `repeat-regions` from one template). Volume over completed outcomes and a weighted conversion rate is `grid.metric-stack` (fixture `metric-stack-volume`). A KPI tile beside a waffle is `grid.panels` (fixture `kpi-and-waffle`).

## Metric stack

Set `stack: {}` to draw two to five panels in top-down order. Shared source counts produce both the marks and the left readouts. The optional period row, partial states, maturing scope and comparison windows belong to the grid. Each panel starts at zero on an independent scale.

A sum uses one or more source measures; a multi-measure column is stacked. A rate divides the summed numerator by its denominator and multiplies by 100. `readout: "change"` gives whole-percent change of averages per category, or the difference of weighted rates after rounding each to one decimal. `readout: { base: "source-id" }` gives a weighted mature step rate and a remaining-per-100 chain. The table gives the formulas.

| Readout | Headline | Span |
|---|---|---|
| `change`, sum measure | `(compare mean per category / base mean per category - 1) × 100`, rounded to whole percent | Base mean → compare mean, divided by the panel `divisor` and rounded to the panel `decimals` (whole counts by default), as the column labels print |
| `change`, rate measure | Compare rate minus base rate, after each weighted rate is rounded to one decimal; rounded to one decimal pp | Base rate → compare rate, each rounded once from the unrounded weighted rate to the panel `decimals` (one by default) |
| `{ "base": "measure-id" }`, rate measure | `100 × sum(numerator) / sum(denominator)` over mature categories, rounded to one decimal percent | `100 × sum(denominator) / sum(base)` → `100 × sum(numerator) / sum(base)` over the same categories |

All sums use the source counts that draw the marks. Rates are weighted by volume, never the mean of the displayed category rates. The remaining-per-100 span uses one decimal, and a starting 100 prints as 100. A zero denominator or a missing input gives `n/a`, not zero.

The stack is refused when a comparison window holds a partial or maturing category, when a partial category is in the maturing band, when the periods do not cover the categories once in order, or when a state scope skips a panel. A step chain is refused when its panels do not share one base measure and one state scope, or when a numerator exceeds its denominator.

Set `data.windows.grain` to day, week, month, quarter or year to name the average unit. Without it, all category ids must match YYYY-MM for month, W01 or YYYY-W01 for week, Q1 or YYYY-Q1 for quarter, or YYYY for year. Week and quarter letters are case-insensitive. Other ids use “average per category”. Window labels do not set the grain. The change header appears only with change readouts.

Use one readout method in each stack: every panel uses `change`, or every panel uses `{ base: "source-id" }`. A base readout stack must form one step chain from the same base measure and use the same state scopes. Do not mix the two methods.

Default plot heights are 200 px for a single-measure column, 150 px for a stacked column, and 130 px for a line. These are minimum defaults: the engine increases them when names, units or readouts need more room. An authored fixed canvas with spare height expands the plots proportionally. `stack.heights` sets explicit plot heights; `rows` sets proportional weights based on the space the labels need.

Use `stack.heights` for plot heights or `rows` for proportional heights. The engine reserves label space and shares one readout gutter and one panel gap. Side margins stay at most 24 px; an authored `margin` still wins. Where the gutter leaves too little room for the values, each readout moves above its panel and the plot takes the full width. Where even the full width is too little, values and category names thin to every second category, counted back from the latest, and the latest value always shows; a hidden name keeps its tick. A stacked panel keys its measures inside its readout; when its segment values do not all fit, none show and the key says that the labels show totals. Provisional columns are hatched in their own paint inside a dashed outline. It refuses dimensions that cause collisions. The maturing band covers all gaps between its scoped panels and ends at their last baseline. `reading.metricStack.readouts[]` exposes the inputs, `method` and `grain`. Count changes use `average-change`; rate changes use `rounded-rate-change`; step rates use `weighted-rate`. Every readout uses the explicit or inferred grain described above, with category as the fallback. Fixtures `metric-stack-volume` and `metric-stack-steps` show both full exhibits.

```json
{
  "type": "grid",
  "data": {
    "categories": [
      { "id": "jan", "label": "Jan" },
      { "id": "feb", "label": "Feb" },
      { "id": "mar", "label": "Mar" },
      { "id": "apr", "label": "Apr", "partial": true }
    ],
    "measures": [
      { "id": "started", "label": "Started", "values": [800, 1000, 1100, 250] },
      { "id": "finished", "label": "Finished", "values": [160, 170, 121, null] }
    ],
    "panels": [
      {
        "id": "volume",
        "type": "column",
        "title": "Started",
        "unit": "cases per month",
        "measure": { "sum": ["started"] },
        "readout": "change"
      },
      {
        "id": "rate",
        "type": "line",
        "title": "Completion",
        "unit": "% of started cases",
        "measure": { "numerator": ["finished"], "denominator": "started" },
        "readout": "change",
        "emphasis": true
      }
    ],
    "states": {
      "maturing": { "from": "mar", "to": "mar", "panels": ["rate"] },
      "partial": { "panels": ["rate"] }
    },
    "windows": {
      "base": { "from": "jan", "to": "jan", "label": "January" },
      "compare": { "from": "feb", "to": "feb", "label": "February" }
    }
  },
  "options": {
    "stack": {},
    "size": { "width": 900 },
    "title": "Starts rise while completion falls",
    "source": "Invented example"
  }
}
```

## Sizing

Floor 280 × 270 px (480 px wide when a panel chart has no compact floor; when that refuses, the compact form stacks an authored grid of several columns in one column and draws down to the width its widest panel measures); fit `fill`.

Below the floor a render is refused with `size-below-floor` and the pixels it needs. `measure` returns the natural and comfortable size for a given spec; see [Sizing in the manual](../manual.md#sizing).
